description: This case study analysis asks when integrating the United Kingdom's energy networks across vectors would outperform running electricity, gas, heat and hydrogen networks separately. It was carried out for the Energy Technologies Institute (ETI) in its 2050 Energy Infrastructure Outlook, with reports by I. Walker and T. Staw published in 2017 and now held by the UK Energy Research Centre Energy Data Centre. The motive was that future energy systems may use infrastructure very differently, since several vectors can deliver the same services, and that integration could make the system more flexible and resilient while meeting carbon targets at lower cost. The work used a case study approach across a range of overarching energy system pathways, with a separate deliverable assessing local cases, to identify the system conditions, geographies and timescales where multi-vector systems make sense. Coverage is Great Britain with local case areas. The summary and local case reports are accessible as PDF documents from the UKERC Energy Data Centre at no cost. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): Energy Technologies Institute Open Licence for Materials. Simulation uses are long-term planning of integrated, resilient multi-vector networks.
